coordinates.note: The ANTARES Collaboration detector paper (NIM A 656 (2011) 11, arXiv:1104.1607) states in a footnote 42 deg 48 min N, 6 deg 10 min E for the detector (42.8 N, 6.17 E, given to 1 arcminute). The 2025 detector paper (arXiv:2504.09473) gives only the depth (2475 m) and the offshore distance (40 km from Toulon). The KM3NeT Letter of Intent (arXiv:1601.07459) places ORCA at 42 48 N 06 02 E, approximately 10 km west of the ANTARES site, consistent with this position.
coordinates.quote: The ANTARES detector, located 40 km offshore from Toulon at 2475 m depth6 , was completed on 29 May 2008, making it the largest neutrino telescope in the northern hemisphere ... 6 42◦ 48N, 6◦ 10E

depth.quote: in a site located 40 km offshore from Toulon (France) and anchored at 2475 m depth.

name: ANTARES site (Mediterranean Sea, off Toulon)
notes: The detector is not attached to a facility record. According to the two-decades ANTARES paper, the onshore control building was at the Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer; it has no separate record in the Atlas.

summary.plain: A patch of seabed in the Mediterranean Sea, about 40 kilometres off the coast of Toulon, France, nearly 2.5 kilometres below the surface. Here the ANTARES neutrino telescope hung its cables of light sensors from 2006 until it was switched off in 2022.
summary.technical: Deep-sea site 40 km offshore from Toulon, France, at 2475 m depth in the Mediterranean Sea, hosting the ANTARES 12-line neutrino telescope from first-line deployment (2006) to shutdown (2022).
